text.en: Think of the last long trip your family took. How far did you go and how long did it take? Long ago people travelled on foot, with animals, and in boats. Today there are so many vehicles that we need big numbers to count them.

Welcome to the first chapter, We the Travellers. To count things like the vehicles in a state we need numbers bigger than a thousand.
Start with 1,000 and keep adding a thousand: 1,000, 2,000, 3,000 and so on up to 9,000. Add one more thousand and we get ten thousand, written 10,000.
Our place value chart gets one more column. From the right the columns are Ones, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands and now Ten Thousands, written TTh. Each column is worth ten times the one on its right.
So 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand and 10 thousands make 1 ten thousand.
We use the same ten digits, 0 to 9, in every place. For example 1,380 is 1 thousand, 3 hundreds, 8 tens and 0 ones. And 9,123 is 9 thousands, 1 hundred, 2 tens and 3 ones.
A comma helps us read big numbers easily. Numbers beyond ten thousand are written the same way: 10,001 is ten thousand one, 10,024 is ten thousand twenty-four, and 13,520 is thirteen thousand five hundred twenty.
To read a number, first read the thousands part and then the rest. 45,867 is forty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-seven.
(additional, not in the textbook) In India we also use the word lakh. 100 thousands make one lakh, written 1,00,000, and the commas go after the first three digits from the right and then after every two digits.

problem.en: Write 20,869 in words and tell the value of 8.

text.en: Split it with the comma: 20 thousand and 869.

why.en: The comma separates the thousands part from the rest.

text.en: Read 869 as eight hundred sixty-nine, so the number is twenty thousand eight hundred sixty-nine.

why.en: Read the thousands part first, then the hundreds, tens and ones.

text.en: The digit 8 is in the hundreds column of 869, so its value is 800.

why.en: The value of a digit depends on its column.

prompt.en: A friend says 10,010 is read as ten thousand ten. Is that right? Explain how you read big numbers.

requiredIdeas.en: Read the thousands part first and then the rest
Use the place value chart with TTh, Th, H, T, O

commonMisconceptions.en: Reading digit by digit like one, zero, zero, one, zero

points.en: 10 thousands make one ten thousand, written 10,000.
The place value columns are O, T, H, Th and TTh, each ten times the one before.
Use a comma to read large numbers, and read the thousands part first.
